newsitem.title: USA: IBM unit to use SEEC Year 2000 software.
newsitem.headline: IBM unit to use SEEC Year 2000 software.

text.p: SEEC Inc on Tuesday said that it has licensed its Year 2000 software to International Business Machines Corp's IBM Global Services Division.
Financial details of the deal were not disclosed.

SEEC said that as part of the non-exclusive license, IBM may use SEEC's COBOL Analyst 2000 and Smart Change 2000 products in any of its "Transformation 2000" factories, excluding those in eastern Europe, Japan and Pakistan.
IBM Global Services will pay SEEC on a per line of code basis, with pricing dependent on whether the tools are used for find or fix, or for the entire Year 2000 conversion process.
SEEC said IBM placed the software in factory sites located in Endicott, N.Y.; Chicago; San Jose, Calif.; and Charlotte, N.C.
SEEC will provide training and technical support for these and any additional factory sites.

The year 2000 problem arises from the two-digit date fields encoded into many computer systems and software. When the year 2000 changes over, these systems may misinterpret the "00" date field as "1900," and crash or lose data.
